title: v1: launch and status with TOML config, matching the current shell launcher
description:
## Why

Replace a personal shell launcher that grew Python snippets and broke twice. The launcher already makes the decision rota exists for; it needs to become a tested Rust tool with its personal details moved into a config file.

## Scope

- Backends:
  - agy (Antigravity CLI);
  - an sclaude-style second Claude account: `claude` run with its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`;
  - Codex (`codex` with its own `CODEX_HOME`);
  - OpenCode;
  - the main Claude config as a last fallback.
- Quota readers per backend, borrowing the approaches in docs/references.md (caam, T3 Code's usage readers, OpenCode's Go usage schema, Codex's RateLimitSnapshot).
- One-at-a-time caps per backend through a process scan or a lock.
- Round-robin across available backends.
- Role and level to model (and effort) mapping in TOML.
- The guard check: refuse a backend whose configured command guard (for example dcg) is not installed.
- An atomic trusted-folder edit where a CLI needs it (agy stops at a trust prompt for an untrusted folder).
- `rota status --json`.
- `rota launch --dry-run`.

## Behavior reference

The reference is the personal shell launcher `agent-launch.sh` (kept outside this repository). Its behavior, without its personal paths or numbers:

- Usage: `[--role implement|review] [--level medium|high] [--only BACKEND] [--dry-run] <prompt file>`, run from the agent's working directory. Bad options or a missing prompt file exit 2.
- Level picks the model or effort: high maps to the top model or effort on each backend, medium to the next one down.
- Role picks the allowed backends: implementers may use agy, the second Claude account and Codex; reviewers only agy and the second Claude account. `--only` narrows the set and must be allowed for the role.
- Each backend check yields available or not, plus a reading line:
  - agy: requires the dcg guard hook in agy's hooks config, then reads `agy -p /usage` (tab-separated lines: group, limit name, "<n>%", reset time) and needs the five-hour and weekly remaining percentages of the "Claude and GPT models" group at or above per-role minimums.
  - Second Claude account: requires stored credentials; probes the usage endpoint with the stored access token; if the probe fails, wakes the account with one tiny prompt and probes again (never in a dry run, which must not spend a turn). Needs five-hour and seven-day used percentages under per-role limits; a missing window counts as under.
  - Codex: refuses in folders configured as belonging to another (work) account, runs an account check, then needs every quota window above 0% remaining.
- Caps: the second Claude account and agy each allow one running session at a time. A running session is found by scanning processes (the claude executable with that `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, including through a symlinked path; any agy process except a /usage probe).
- Round-robin: keeps the last pick in a state file and takes the first available backend after it, in a fixed order.
- No backend available: reviews and `--only` refuse (exit 3) with all readings; implementers fall back to the main Claude config, logged loudly.
- Every decision is logged with time, folder, role, level and all readings.
- `--dry-run` prints the pick and the command (the prompt shown as `$(cat file)`) and changes nothing, including the state file.
- Before launching agy, adds the folder to agy's `trustedWorkspaces` setting with an atomic write that keeps other keys and the file mode.
- Codex runs interactive and unattended, with approvals and sandbox off; the guard hook still checks every command.
- The launch replaces the launcher process (exec).

## Out of scope

- Mid-session failover.
- Account switching within one provider.
- Eon integration.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests for each quota parser, with fixtures of made-up data.
- Unit tests for the rotation and the caps.
- Unit tests for config validation.
- A dry run that matches the shell script's decision on the same readings.
- An example config in the repository with placeholder values only; personal paths, accounts and thresholds live in the user's config file.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test`
- One real launch of each backend in a scratch folder.

- rota-89n.2: 1694f07, fixture-backed readers, guards/caps and status.
- rota-89n.3: f69a230, launch/atomic persistence/dry-run and documentation.

Two fresh read-only Codex reviews ran sequentially, with full parent/child specs and README principles in independent briefs:
- Review 1: full 11c2bee..f69a230. Six blockers: empty quota permission, fresh cap checks, executable aliases, deadline through pipe drain, decimal exclusive cutoffs and exported workspace metadata. Fixed in da5feae, with status suggestions included.
- Review 2: full 11c2bee..da5feae. Three blockers: unusable Eon snapshot state, wrapped/interpreted runtime identity and invalid argument encoding. Fixed in 2067f4e; state-write ordering and redundant-scan suggestions also addressed.
- Narrow round 1 confirmed the original quota/deadline/privacy/status fixes and found one direct regression: relative interpreted script paths used the launcher's working directory. Fixed in 520cf6a by using each process's working directory for script/account paths; regression tests use differing directories.
- Final narrow round 2 (through 520cf6a): all remaining findings fixed; no blocking findings remain. Synthetic status/dry-run checks verified fresh-state gating, wrapped identities, cross-directory scripts/account aliases and invalid-input exit 2. Both bounded narrow rounds completed; no further broad review was run.

Author verification after fixes: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test (23 tests); git diff --check. Live dry-run comparison passed 8/8 role/level/--only combinations, matching exits, picks and shell-parsed command arguments. No rota state/log/lock/trust changes from dry-run. title: Validated TOML configuration and pure routing core
description:
## Why
The binary is a stub. Routing must first have a validated personal-detail-free schema and a pure decision function.

## Evidence
- src/main.rs only prints usage; Cargo.toml has no dependencies.
- README.md requires explicit fallback, backend caps and config-owned personal details.

## Scope
Implement src/config.rs, src/decision.rs, example config and unit tests. The parent rota-89n defines behavior. Include enabled backends, role/level commands and environment, command guards, reader choices, limits, process-cap definitions, fallback and state/log paths. Do not execute agent commands in this slice.

## Acceptance
TOML validation rejects ambiguous/invalid routing and command definitions. The pure core filters roles and --only, rotates after the last pick, respects caps, rejects unknown quotas unless explicitly permitted and only falls back for implementers without --only. Refusals expose exit 3; invalid arguments expose exit 2. All config examples and tests use invented data.

## Implementation Notes
Keep backend names generic. OpenCode model and variant are command configuration. Reader and guard commands permit existing tools and proxy env without building a proxy. Missing Claude windows may be explicitly allowed.

## Verification
cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test. Record proof, close and sync before the slice commit.

## Stop Conditions
Escalate incompatible parent requirements or unexpected external changes.

## Maintenance Notes
No mid-session failover or account switching. Personal configuration stays outside the repository.

comments.text: Implemented validated TOML config, placeholder-only example and pure routing core. Proof: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test passed (5 tests: schema validation, rotation/roles/caps, fallback/refusal, quota boundaries/missing/unknown). No agent commands executed.

title: Quota readers, guard checks, process readings and status
description:
## Why
Routing needs reliable quota, guard and activity readings before any launch can be allowed.

## Evidence
The parent rota-89n describes agy tab-separated usage, Claude subscription usage, eon workspace quota and explicit unknown-quota handling for OpenCode.

## Scope
Add quota readers, guard/account checks, Linux process scanning and rota status [--json]. Reader commands and parser kinds come from config. Test parsers with invented fixtures, including missing and malformed windows. Do not launch an agent.

## Acceptance
Support agy usage, Claude endpoint JSON and existing helper text, eon Codex and main Claude quota. Command failures and malformed data refuse safely. Guard requirements are checked before quota probes; caps count any matching backend process, including reviewers and canonicalized account-directory symlinks. OpenCode remains unavailable with unknown quota unless explicitly enabled and allowed. Status exposes readings, counts and availability in text or JSON. Never refresh an account during status or dry-run.

## Implementation Notes
Use existing external reader commands rather than duplicating network authentication. Apply bounded timeouts. Environment and excluded folders are configured. The parent defines role limits and fallback behavior.

## Verification
cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test. Record proof, close and sync before the slice commit.

## Stop Conditions
Escalate incompatible parent requirements or unexpected external changes.

## Maintenance Notes
No personal paths, account identifiers or thresholds in repo fixtures or beads.

title: Launch, atomic persistence, dry-run parity and documentation
description:
## Why
The validated router and readers must replace the shell launcher while preserving dry-run safety and atomic writes.

## Evidence
The parent rota-89n specifies launch, atomic state and trusted-folder edits, decision logging, command exec and shell parity.

## Scope
Implement rota launch CLI, safe dry-run rendering, serialized selection, atomic state/trust writes, decision log and exec. Update README.md for actual usage and configuration. Create personal config outside the repository and compare dry-run decisions/commands with the reference launcher. No real agent launch is authorized in this implementation session.

## Acceptance
Bad options and missing prompt exit 2; unavailable review/--only exit 3. Dry-run prints the selected backend and command and changes no files. Real launch code rechecks caps under a launch lock, logs decisions and loud fallback, preserves other trusted-settings keys and mode, writes state atomically and execs the configured command. Per-backend environment supports proxies; OpenCode command contains its configured model#variant. External configuration matches reference roles, levels, order and guards. Parity covers both roles/levels and --only codex, listing intentional differences. Real launches are deferred to the coordinator.

## Implementation Notes
Follow the parent's behavior and newer user decisions. Never wake the busy second Claude account during implementation or parity work. Keep personal configuration and parity artifacts outside the repo.

## Verification
cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test; dry-run parity. Record proof, close and sync before the slice commit. Parent additionally requires two sequential fresh read-only reviews of the full diff, fixes and review ledger.

## Stop Conditions
Escalate incompatible parent requirements or unexpected external changes.

## Maintenance Notes
No real launches, process signaling or pushing. Coordinator performs live backend smoke checks after review.

title: Run headless agent sessions with rota run (plan, review, investigate)
description:
Lucca, 2026-11-06: "we are accumulating shell scripts again. cant we improve rota?" then "do it" to the overseer's proposal: rota absorbs the agent-lifecycle scripts the Eon overseer keeps writing (124 of them that day, 110 one-off copies). Each command must be generic (no Eon paths or policy in code; per-machine values in config.toml), allowlistable once, and shares the session registry planned in rota-1k7.

## What

`rota run`: a headless agent run (plan, review, investigate) for backends that have a non-interactive mode (Codex `codex exec` today; Claude `-p` later).

- Flags: `--role plan|review|investigate`, `--only BACKEND`, `--cwd DIR`, `--brief FILE`, `--effort LEVEL`, `--timeout DURATION`, `--name NAME`, `--sandbox read-only|workspace-write`, repeated `--add-dir DIR`.
- Before running: the backend's guard (as `rota launch` has; for Codex the account pin that codex-account-check.sh does today), quota and cap checks like `launch`.
- Environment: a configurable scrub list (for Eon: unset WAYLAND_DISPLAY, DISPLAY and every EON_* variable, set EON_RUNTIME_DIR to a private dir) so a run never reaches the person's live terminal session.
- stdin closed (a Codex review once hung two hours on stdin), a hard timeout, and the log and final report written under a rota run directory named by the session; the paths are printed and recorded in the session registry.
- Exit status reflects the run's; a timeout is reported as such.

Replaces: eon-overseer/codex-run.sh, codex-review.sh, codex-account-check.sh, start-planners.sh.

## Acceptance
- A run with a closed stdin, a timeout that fires, a guard refusal and a quota refusal, each tested.
- The scrub list removes configured variables and sets configured ones (tested).
- Docs: README usage and config keys.

title: Read agy's 'disabled' quota row as exhausted and show when it resets
description:
## Why

When agy's "Claude and GPT models" weekly window is spent, `agy -p /usage` prints the
five-hour row as `disabled` instead of a percentage:

```
Claude and GPT models	Weekly Limit Remaining	0%	2030-01-08T14:00:00Z
Claude and GPT models	Five Hour Limit Remaining	disabled
```

`quota::parse` (`src/quota.rs`, `Parser::Agy`) rejects that row with
`invalid agy percentage`, so `rota status` shows `quota unreadable` for both roles. The
backend is still refused, but for the wrong reason: the owner cannot tell an exhausted
account from a broken reader, and rota never says when the backend comes back. The real
reason (weekly 0%) and its reset time are both in the output rota already reads.

## What

1. **Parse `disabled` as unavailable.** In the agy parser, a `disabled` value for a known
   window reads as 0% remaining. Any other non-percentage value stays an error.
2. **Keep the reset time.** The agy rows carry an RFC 3339 reset time in the fourth field.
   Keep it for each window, so a refusal can name it. A missing or malformed reset time is
   not an error: the window just has no reset time. Other parsers are unchanged unless
   carrying the reset is free for them.
3. **Show it.** When a role is refused because a window is under its limit, `rota status`
   (and the launch refusal message) names the window and, when known, its reset time, e.g.
   `weekly_left=0% (resets 2030-01-08T14:00:00Z)`. Keep the existing line shape otherwise.

## Out of scope

- Converting the reset to local time, or counting down.
- Reading the Gemini rows, or any change to how limits are configured.

## Verification

- Unit tests in `src/quota.rs` with made-up fixtures: the `disabled` five-hour row parses
  as 0% beside a 0% weekly row; a garbage value (`n/a`) is still an error; a row without a
  reset field parses with no reset.
- A test that the status/refusal text for an exhausted agy fixture names `weekly` and the
  reset time, and does not say `quota unreadable`.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`.
close_reason: Landed as e2d06f5 with proof and review records
